html:
Paramaribo is the capital of Suriname, on the Suriname River near the coast. It grew from an Indigenous village and an English and then Dutch fort, Fort Zeelandia, from the 1600s.

Under Dutch rule it was the port for the sugar, coffee and cacao of the plantations upriver. Its merchants, officials and free people of colour built wooden houses with white walls and green shutters, along streets lined with trees. Its historic centre became a World Heritage Site in 2002. A mosque and a synagogue stand side by side on one street.

Nearly half of Suriname's people live in or near the city. It was the stage for the end of slavery in 1863 and the December murders of 1982 at Fort Zeelandia. It was won by the Dutch under the Treaty of Breda.
sum: Paramaribo is the capital of Suriname, on the Suriname River near the coast. It grew from an Indigenous village and an English and then Dutch fort, Fort Zeelandia, from the 1600s.
